newsitem.title: UK: NWE spot naphtha weak, paper gains resilient.
newsitem.headline: NWE spot naphtha weak, paper gains resilient.

text.p: NWE spot naphtha prices remained weak in thin trade on Wednesday with end-users staying out of the market and offers scarce at the lower levels.

The contango between physical oil and April paper ballooned out to around $7 in early business, flagging perceptions of a seasonal pick-up in gasoline demand, a factor some traders were looking fop to pull naphtha out of the doldrums.
"Gasoline holds they key to the whole thing, but it's ridiculous that anyone would want to pay up to $7 over physical (naphtha) for April paper though, one trader said.
However, the paper market gains were resilient.
Paper dipped only one dollar as both crude and NYMEX gasoline futures slipped from the early highs during the afternoon.

Despite firmer gasoline markets on both sides of the Atlantic traders said there was still little chance of an arbitrage for naphtha although U.S. stocks are some 10.3 million barrels below levels this time last year.

"A $55-60 fob Med-cif Far East spread has seen around 12 cargoes booked from the Med to the east recently but there are few fob offers now at these weaker levels," a trader said. "I'm looking for fob barrels but just can't find any.

Turkey's state oil refining company Tupras said on Wednesday it had sold up to 35,000 tonnes of naphtha to the Swiss trading company Marc Rich Investment AG through a tender at a premium of $6.2 per tonne over benchmark quotes.
On Tuesday a Greek cargo was reported traded at around benchmark high cif quotes +$8 a tonne to a trader. The cargo is expected to go to the Far East.
In NWE open spec cargoes traded early at $186 for 12kt cif NWE and pipeline spec was heard offered around $189 but buying interest from petrochemicals remained relaxed.
